Comments

A comment anchors to whatever it is about — a card, a group, an empty point on the canvas, the board as a whole, or a range of text inside a document. Comments thread, resolve, and support @ mentions that notify the person named. A comments toggle hides all of them when you want to see the board clean.

Updated October 25, 2026

Comments attach to the thing they are about. This is the whole design: feedback that lives in a sidebar, ordered by time, loses the connection to what it referred to within a day.

What you can comment on

AnchorReads as
A card"this image"
A group"this sequence"
An empty point"something should go here"
The board"the whole thing"
A text range in a document"this sentence"

Right-click → Comment, or the rail's + → Annotate → Comment.

Threads

Comments thread with replies. Resolve when the thing is dealt with — resolved comments are archived rather than deleted, so the record of why something changed survives.

Resolving and hiding a comment is for its author and for people who can edit the board; deleting one is for its author. Someone with view-only access sees those buttons on their own comments only.

Mentions

Type @ in a comment to mention someone. They are notified. See Notifications.

You can also mention clusters, documents and cards, which turns a comment into a navigable link rather than a description of where to look.

Hiding them

The comments toggle hides every comment bubble on the board — for you only, not for everyone. Use it when presenting or when the feedback has piled up and you want to see the work.

Bubbles on a crowded board

Comment bubbles lay themselves out to avoid covering the content they refer to and to avoid stacking on each other, so a heavily-reviewed board stays readable.

Who can comment

On the canvas, anyone who can open the board, including viewers. Editing a card is a different right from talking about it, and feedback is the point of sharing a board with someone. Public links are the exception: they are anonymous, and comments need an account.

A comment on a text range is different: it lives inside the document's text, so it follows edit access. A viewer can open a document's comment threads and read them, but adding, replying to, resolving or deleting one needs edit access.

From your own code, or an assistant

The Comments API lists a board's threads, the ones inside its documents included, and adds, resolves and deletes comments under the same rules. Connected over MCP, an assistant can read the feedback on a board, act on it, reply, resolve what it dealt with, and comment on the words of a document.

Comments versus votes

  • A comment is a sentence: reasoning, a request, a decision, with a thread and a record.
  • A vote is a count: which of these, quickly, with no discussion.

If you want to know why, use a comment.

Frequently asked questions

Can I comment on empty canvas?

Yes. A comment can anchor to a point rather than an object, which is how you leave "something should go here".

How do I hide comments for a presentation?

The comments toggle hides every comment bubble on the board. It affects only your view.

Do resolved comments disappear?

They are archived rather than deleted, so the record of a decision survives.
